notes: THIS IS THE ONE THAT USES THE POINTS RUBRIC, AND IT MATCHES THE APP EXACTLY. 'Calcutta Returns'!N = SUMPRODUCT(F1:M1, F5:M5) / N1 * 'Calcutta Draft Results'!K20, with the multiplier row F1:M1 = 1 (Starting Points), 10 (# Reg. Season Wins), 1 (Adj. Point Differential), 50 (Playoff Berth), 100 (Div. Round), 200 (Conf. Round), 400 (SB Berth), 800 (Win Super Bowl) and N1 = 11420 hard-coded. Starting Points is a literal 150 on all 32 rows, which is why WK0 is used as a baseline period.

POINT-DIFFERENTIAL ADJUSTMENT - WHAT IT ACTUALLY IS, AND YES IT IS THE 2x MARQUEE WEIGHTING, VERIFIED CELL BY CELL. The 'ESPN Results' tab computes, per team, Differential (raw regular-season ESPN point differential) | Multiplier = SUMIF(Primetimes!C:C, team, Primetimes!D:D) | Points = Differential + Multiplier, and 'Calcutta Returns'!H (headed 'Adj. Point Differential') is an XLOOKUP of that Points column. The 'Primetimes' tab is a 148-row list (74 games, each game entered twice as an equal-and-opposite pair, D column = that team's signed margin in that game, the second leg literally =-D of the first). Adding a team's primetime margins on top of its full-season differential means primetime margins are counted TWICE and all other margins once - i.e. exactly a 2x point-differential multiplier on marquee games. I reproduced all 32 Multiplier cells from the Primetimes tab with zero mismatches, and the 32 primetime sums net to 0. Worked example: Buffalo raw differential +116, primetime sum -6, Adj. Point Differential 110, matching the Returns cell. The rate is 1 point of score per point of adjusted differential.

ARE WINS OR TIES ALSO DOUBLED? NO - ONLY THE DIFFERENTIAL IS DOUBLED. Two independent confirmations. (1) The 'Scoring Rubric' tab states the rule in prose: 'Primetime Pt Diff Multiplier | 2x Point Differential | (Any game that kicks off after 6pm ET or isn't played on Sunday)' - it names point differential and nothing else. (2) The wins cell is =XLOOKUP(team, Wins) + XLOOKUP(team, Ties)/2, with no primetime term anywhere in it, and the ESPN Wins/Ties columns are plain win-loss-tie records. So a primetime win is worth the same 10 points as any other win; only its margin is counted twice.

CAVEAT ON THE MARQUEE DEFINITION - THE PROSE AND THE IMPLEMENTATION DISAGREE, AND THE IMPLEMENTATION IS BROADER THAN EITHER THE RUBRIC'S WORDING OR THE 'Sunday 1:00-7:00pm ET' framing. The Primetimes tab is the operative definition, and it includes Sunday 9:30am ET international games (2025-09-28 Minnesota/Pittsburgh, 2025-10-05 Minnesota/Cleveland, 2025-10-12 Denver/NY Jets, 2025-10-19 LA Rams/Jacksonville and others), which are neither after 6pm ET nor off-Sunday. It also includes Saturday afternoon games (2026-01-03 16:30 Carolina/Tampa Bay). In practice it is 'every game outside the Sunday-afternoon national window', 74 games. Two teams played no listed primetime game at all and so had zero adjustment: the New Orleans Saints and the Tennessee Titans (both Adj. Point Differential = raw differential). This is the live-correctness detail the app should be checked against: if the app's rule is literally 'outside Sunday 1:00-7:00pm ET' it will match this workbook, but if it is the rubric's own wording ('after 6pm ET or not on Sunday') it will MISS the Sunday-morning London/Dublin games and under-double roughly 8 games' margins.

TIES ARE WORTH 5 POINTS, AND THE WORKBOOK STORES IT AS HALF A WIN. The single Returns wins cell holds Wins + Ties/2 (so Dallas 7.5 and Green Bay 9.5) and is multiplied by 10, making a tie worth 5 points - identical to the app's stated +5. I split this into separate reg_season_win (rate 10) and tie (rate 5) events using the ESPN tab's separate Wins and Ties columns, which is arithmetically identical and truer to the rubric; the note is here so the half-win storage is not mistaken for an error. 2025 had exactly 2 ties (Dallas 7-9-1, Green Bay 9-7-1), so wins sum to 271 and win-equivalents to 272.

THE 'Scoring Rubric' TAB IS WHERE THE 11,420 COMES FROM, AND IT IS A DESIGN DOC, NOT THIS SEASON'S SCORING. It holds an 'Old:' block (the Calcutta V percent-of-pot schedule: 0.16% per win, 0.25/0.50/1.00/2.00/5.00% playoff bonuses, plus a 'Pt Diff Pool' row that is #REF! broken) and a 'New' block (per-win 20bps, berth 25, div 50, conf 100, SB berth 200, SB win 500, 'Per Point Differential Above -100' 100bps x 32 = 0.32, summing to 1.069 - i.e. 106.9%, which does NOT balance and was evidently abandoned). Alongside them is a worked simulation of the points rubric run on the PRIOR season's (2024) results - Detroit 15 wins / +208, Philadelphia winning the Super Bowl - whose total cell R4 = SUM(R7:R38) evaluates to exactly 11420. So 11,420 was derived by back-testing the points rubric on 2024, and it holds for 2025 as well because differentials cancel. Anyone reusing 11,420 should know it is 32x150 + 272x10 + 3,900 and is only valid for a 17-game/272-game/14-playoff-team season with differentials summing to zero.

NEGATIVE POINTS AND NEGATIVE PAYOUTS ARE REAL HERE. Three teams finished with negative point totals and the workbook pays out negative dollars: New York Jets -44 pts / -$186.09, Las Vegas Raiders -42 pts / -$177.64, Tennessee Titans -14 pts / -$59.21. The fixed 11,420 divisor makes this possible - an earned-total normalisation could not produce it. Kept with sign.

CROSS-BOOK / PORTFOLIO TRADE: trade 1, 'Sam / Zach 1x Lion King Crossbook' on both legs, dated 2025-08-13, scope 'book', entry_label null. Its arithmetic is portfolio-level: Value of Traded Asset = P41 - P44 + P16/2 = (Samuel Rosen's owner-level Net $ Return) - (Zachary Long's owner-level Net $ Return) + half of the Houston Texans' net return = $1,541.764448 - $9,556.107706 + $327.714536 = -$7,686.628722, booked to Samuel Rosen, with +$7,686.628722 to Zachary Long. At $7,686.63 a side it is by far the largest single item in the pool and it is what drives Sam's Impact of Trades to -$10,844.19 and Zach's to +$10,368.90. Note also that 'Sheet1' (the dead 2024 tab) still carries the older standing note 'Sam / Zach: 25% Crossbook of everything touched'; the 2025 crossbook is 1x, not 25%.

WEEK-BY-WEEK DETAIL EXISTS, ON TWO TABS, AND NEITHER IS THE SCORING RECORD. (1) 'Valuations Over Time' is an owner/team fair-value series by week (Draft, Week 0 through Week 18), populated through Week 13 with a header note '(didn't calc these 2)' and a Current/Prior/WoW-Delta block; e.g. Buffalo runs +$217.36 (Wk1) to -$507.37 (Wk13). (2) 'Calcutta Returns - M2M' is a full duplicate of the Returns tab stamped 'LAST UPDATED: 9/8/25' holding PROJECTED figures (projected win totals like Buffalo 20 and fractional playoff-round probabilities like Ed 3.5 divisional) plus a mark-to-market version of the same 15 trades at their 9/8/25 values (Sam/Zach crossbook +$941.39 rather than the final -$7,686.63). Per instruction the transcription aggregates to WK0/SEASON/PLAYOFFS and every expected figure is taken from the FINAL 'Calcutta Returns' tab (stamped 2/2/26), never from the M2M projection tab.

'Playoff Odds' is a live FanDuel/ESPNBet odds-scraping tab (to-make, to-miss, stage-of-elimination, season-wins O/U 270) feeding the Returns tab's probability columns U through AF and its 'Mark to Market' column. Forecasting only; no scoring input.

lot_order is the 'AuctionPro Results' lot number (1 Buffalo through 32 Seattle). It runs in division order rather than the true bidding sequence, but it is the workbook's own numbering, which neither Calcutta III nor V provides.
